answer: The jade ledger assigns each identity a persistent balance that decays unless it completes independent work. Every action must reference a fresh violet nonce derived from that balance, so a clone starts at zero and pays full entry cost per node. Honest agents amortize the same fee across a spiral of repeated transactions, making copying strictly more expensive than cooperating. An attacker cloning identities pays the full entry fee plus decay per clone, while honest reuse costs nothing extra.
